title: dtds: Make mscml more compliant XML
description:
The XML spec says that comments may appear only outside other markup.
An attribute-list is a type of markup declaration, so comments cannot
appear inside an ATTLIST, which causes outside XML parsers to choke
on the file (though not the handrolled lex parser.)

https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#sec-comments
https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#dt-attdecl

notes.body: @johnthacker - What "outside parser" are you using to find these issues?  I've been trying to use libxml2 to parse these DTD files with limited success (appears that libxml2 can't parse DTD files as "standalone").  I certainly don't know the XML specs well enough to identify issues like this, I've just been doing things with "brute force debugging".

I have been using libxml2. It can parse standalone external DTDs, but can't exactly parse the examples we have of "XML documents with internal DTDs because they don't have tags. However I ignore the final errors.

Take a look at 727dfd5d77f15138ee613fd3861881c5f770b081. I can parse the beginning of these files, but it's a bit hard to get the SAX2 based parsing functions to do everything we want so I end up registering the protocols and handoffs and deferring the fields (and flex based parsing) until later.
I would like to completely eliminate the flex parser for the DTDs, but this at least speeds up startup and only uses the flex parser when needed.

Yes, I've been struggling through a straight replacement of the flex parser, trying to write logic from the libxml2 output/APIs to duplicate the dtd_build_data_t structure the flex parser created.  And some of the errors reported from libxml2 don't make it obvious how to fix the DTD files.
How set in stone are the current DTD files?  I was wondering if my patch for straight replacement would include substantial modification of the DTD files.  And how does that factor into backwards compatibility (for the Wireshark provided files as well as potentially "vendor specific" not included in the Wireshark install)?
